extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and supervisory patent examiners; patent applicants and practitioners
extracted.subtask_short: patent examination citation and office actions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners on drafting Office actions, citing prior art, providing copies of cited references, and procedural steps for examination (including duties of primary and supervisory examiners). Covers bibliographic requirements, forms (PTO‑326, PTO‑892), and electronic access (Private PAIR / E‑Patent Reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any inquiry concerning this communication or earlier communications from the examiner should be directed to [1] whose telephone number is [2]. The examiner can normally be reached on [3] from [4] to [5]. The examiner can also be reached on alternate [6]. If attempts to reach the examiner by telephone are unsuccessful, the examiner’s supervisor, [7], can be reached on [8]. The fax phone number for the organization where this application or proceeding is assigned is 571-273-8300.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bracketed template in Office actions; insert examiner name, area code/phone, regular work days, duty hours, alternate contact, SPE name and SPE phone. Provide clear contact information so inquiries are directed appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute cited in prior action (¶7.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the text of sections of Title 35, U.S. Code was previously reproduced in an Office action, form paragraph 7.103 may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If statute sections were reproduced in a prior Office action, refer readers to that prior action using form paragraph 7.103 rather than repeating statutory text in the current action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for Reply and consequences (PTO‑326)
rubrics_metrics.description: A SHORTENED STATUTORY PERIOD FOR REPLY IS SET TO EXPIRE MONTH(S) OR THIRTY (30) DAYS, WHICHEVER IS LONGER, FROM THE MAILING DATE OF THIS COMMUNICATION. If NO period for reply is specified above, the maximum statutory period will apply and will expire SIX (6) MONTHS from the mailing date of this communication. Extensions of time may be available under the provisions of 37 CFR 1.136(a). In no event, however, may a reply be timely filed after SIX (6) MONTHS from the mailing date of this communication. Failure to reply within the set or extended period for reply will, by statute, cause the application to become ABANDONED (35 U.S.C. § 133). Any reply received by the Office later than three months after the mailing date of this communication, even if timely filed, may reduce any earned patent term adjustment. See 37 CFR 1.704(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office Action Summary (PTO‑326) must state the reply period clearly, note availability of extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a), and warn of abandonment/term adjustment consequences. Use the prescribed statutory wording and timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action status and Quayle disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Status options in Office Action Summary include: Responsive to communication(s) filed on [date]. This action is FINAL. This action is non-final. Since this application is in condition for allowance except for formal matters, prosecution as to the merits is closed in accordance with the practice under Ex parte Quayle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly indicate whether the action is final or non‑final, whether responsive to prior filings, and when Ex parte Quayle practice (closure of merits for formal matters) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Office Action Summary must indicate claim status: Claim(s) is/are pending in the application; Of the above claim(s) is/are withdrawn from consideration; Claim(s) is/are allowed; Claim(s) is/are rejected; Claim(s) is/are objected to; Claim(s) are subject to restriction and/or election requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each claim, state its disposition using the listed categories so the applicant understands which claims are pending, withdrawn, allowed, rejected, objected to, or restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application papers objections and drawing replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification is objected to by the Examiner. The drawing(s) filed on [date] is/are: accepted or objected to by the Examiner. Applicant may not request that any objection to the drawing(s) be held in abeyance. Replacement drawing sheet(s) including the correction is required if the drawing(s) is objected to. See 37 CFR 1.121(d). The oath or declaration is objected to by the Examiner. Note the attached Office Action or form PTO‑152.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When objecting to specification, drawings, or oath/declaration, state the objection and cite the applicable CFR; require replacement drawing sheets when drawings are objected to and disallow requests to hold drawing objections in abeyance (citing 37 CFR 1.85(a) as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority acknowledgment and certified copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgment is made of a claim for foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. § 119(a)-(d) or (f). Certified copies of the priority documents have been received. Certified copies of the priority documents have been received in Application No. [ ]. Copies of the certified copies of the priority documents have been received in this National Stage application from the International Bureau (PCT Rule 17.2(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether foreign priority is claimed and whether certified priority documents have been received; if not received, list which certified copies are missing and attach details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments to Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment examples in Office Action Summary include: Notice of References Cited (PTO‑892); Notice of Draftsperson’s Patent Drawing Review (PTO‑948); Information Disclosure Statement(s) (PTO/SB/08); Interview Summary (PTO‑413); Notice of Informal Patent Application; Other specified attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List attachments by name and paper number/mail date so the applicant knows what documents accompany the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner review responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: After the search has been completed, action is taken in the light of the references found. Where the assistant examiner has been in the Office but a short time, it is the duty of the primary examiner to review the application thoroughly. The assistant examiner should explain the invention and discuss the references regarded as most pertinent. The primary examiner may indicate the action to be taken, whether restriction or election of species is to be required, or whether the claims are to be considered on their merits. If action on the merits is to be given, the primary examiner may indicate how the references are to be applied in cases where the claim is to be rejected, or authorize allowance if it is not met in the references and no further field of search is known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiners must personally review applications, mentor new assistant examiners, decide on restriction/election, apply references for rejections, and authorize allowances when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory examiner pendency oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The supervisory patent examiners are expected to personally check on the pendency of every application which is up for the third or subsequent Office action with a view to finally concluding its prosecution. Any application that has been pending five years should be carefully studied by the supervisory patent examiner and every effort should be made to terminate its prosecution. The application is to be considered “special” by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisors must monitor third‑action and long‑pending (5+ years) applications and take steps to conclude prosecution, treating such applications as special to reduce pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required bibliographic data when citing references (37 CFR 1.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: If domestic patents are cited by the examiner, their numbers and dates, and the names of the patentees will be stated. If domestic patent application publications are cited, their publication number, publication date, and the names of the applicants will be stated. If foreign published applications or patents are cited, their nationality or country, numbers and dates, and the names of the patentees will be stated, and such other data will be furnished as may be necessary to enable identification. If printed publications are cited, the author (if any), title, date, pages or plates, and place of publication, or place where a copy can be found, will be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing any reference, provide sufficient bibliographic detail (numbers, dates, names, pagination, place of publication or repository) so that the applicant (or patent owner) can identify and retrieve the cited material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal knowledge rejections and affidavit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection in an application is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an employee of the Office, the data shall be as specific as possible, and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee, and such affidavit shall be subject to contradiction or explanation by the affidavits of the applicant and other persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague factual assertions based on personal knowledge; provide specific supporting data and be prepared to furnish an employee affidavit if the applicant requests it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite pertinent prior art and explain relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: During the examination of an application or reexamination of a patent, the examiner should cite appropriate prior art which is nearest to the subject matter defined in the claims. When such prior art is cited, its pertinence should be explained. The examiner must consider all the prior art references (alone and in combination) cited in the application or reexamination, including those cited by the applicant in a properly submitted Information Disclosure Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the closest prior art, state why it is pertinent (explain the relevance in the record, e.g., bracketed explanation using form paragraph 7.96), and consider combinations of references and applicant‑submitted IDS entries (see MPEP §609).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search based on actual filing date and citing post‑parent art
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should search all applications based on the actual U.S. filing date of the application rather than on the filing date of any parent U.S. application for which benefit/priority is claimed. Examiners should cite of interest all material prior art having an effective filing date after the filing date of the U.S. parent application but before the actual filing date of the application being examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to 20‑year patent term rules, searches must use the actual filing date; identify and cite intervening art filed after the parent but before the child application's actual filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art listing at allowance and 'None' notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed applications should generally contain a citation of pertinent prior art for printing in the patent, even if no claim presented during the prosecution was considered unpatentable over such prior art. Only in those instances where a proper search has not revealed any prior art relevant to the claimed invention is it appropriate to send an application to issue with no art cited. In the case where no prior art is cited, the examiner must write “None” on a form PTO‑892 and insert it in the file wrapper. Where references have been cited during prosecution of parent applications and a continuing application, having no newly cited references, is ready for allowance, the cited references of the parent applications should be listed on form PTO‑892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At allowance include pertinent prior art for printing; if none exists, explicitly record “None” on PTO‑892. For continuations, carry forward parent citations to the continuing application's PTO‑892.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of copies of cited references and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of foreign patent documents and non‑patent literature references (except as noted) are automatically furnished without charge to applicant together with the Office action in which they are cited. Copies of the cited references are also placed in the application file for examiner use. Copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications are not provided in paper to applicants and are not placed in the application file. Copies of references cited by applicant in accordance with MPEP § 609, § 707.05(b), and § 708.02 are not furnished to applicant with the Office action. Additionally, copies of references cited in continuation applications if they had been previously cited in the parent application are not furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Furnish paper copies of foreign patents/NPL with the Office action except for listed exceptions (applicant‑cited refs, parent‑provided refs, and U.S. patents/publications). Check PTO‑892 columns to determine whether a copy is to be furnished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to ensure cited references are furnished (PTO‑892 workflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist in providing copies of, or access to, references, the examiner should: (A) Type the citation of the references on form PTO‑892, “Notice of References Cited” using OACS; (B) Place the form PTO‑892 in the front of the file wrapper; (C) Include in the application file wrapper all of the references cited by the examiner which are to be furnished to the applicant; (D) Turn the application in to the technical support staff for counting. Any application which is handed in without all of the required references will be returned to the examiner. The missing reference(s) should be obtained and the file returned to the technical support staff as quickly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the (A)–(D) checklist to ensure referenced documents are properly recorded, placed in the file, and provided to the applicant; coordinate with technical support for counting and inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: E‑Patent Reference access and steps for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The E‑Patent Reference feature is accessed using a button on the Private PAIR screen. Access to Private PAIR is required to utilize E‑Patent Reference. The Office urges practitioners and applicants not represented by a practitioner to: (1) obtain a no‑cost USPTO PKI digital certificate; (2) obtain a USPTO customer number; (3) associate pending and new application filings with their customer number; (4) install free software required to access Private PAIR and E‑Patent Reference; and (5) make appropriate arrangements for Internet access. Instructions for obtaining a PKI certificate, customer number, associating customer number, downloading software (and need for Adobe Reader), and recommending high‑speed Internet are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants (especially unrepresented) should follow the five steps to obtain Private PAIR/E‑Patent Reference access so they can download cited U.S. patents/publications in PDF. Provide links and contact numbers (EBC, help desk) as given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling applicant‑submitted prior art and IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP § 609 sets forth guidelines for applicants, their attorneys and agents who desire to submit prior art for consideration by the USPTO. Submitted citations will not in any way diminish the obligation of examiners to conduct independent prior art searches, or relieve examiners of citing other pertinent prior art of which they may be aware. Prior art submitted by applicant in the manner provided in MPEP § 609 will not be supplied with an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept applicant‑submitted citations per MPEP §609 but continue independent searching; do not automatically furnish applicant‑submitted citations with Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and listing of references on PTO‑892
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing references for the first time, the identifying data of the citation should be placed on form PTO‑892, “Notice of References Cited,” a copy of which will be attached to the Office action. No distinction is to be made between references on which a claim is rejected and those formerly referred to as “pertinent.” Where an applicant in an amendatory paper refers to a reference that is subsequently relied upon by the examiner, such reference shall be cited by the examiner in the usual manner using form PTO‑892, unless applicant has listed the reference on a form PTO/SB/08 that has been initialed by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always enter identifying data on PTO‑892 for first citations, attach PTO‑892 to the Office action, and use PTO‑892 for applicant‑referenced material unless PTO/SB/08 was used and initialed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation data requirements — U.S. patents and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a U.S. patent application publication is cited by the examiner, the publication number, publication date, name of the applicant, class, and subclass should be cited under the section “U.S. Patent Documents” on form PTO‑892. For U.S. patents, the patent number, patent date, name of the patentee, class and subclass should also be cited. Examiners are encouraged to cite the kind codes printed on U.S. patent application publications and patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide patent/publication number, date, applicant/patentee name, and classification (class/subclass) and include kind codes where applicable to facilitate accurate identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation data requirements — foreign patents
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing foreign patents, the patent number, kind code, citation date, name of the country, name of the patentee, and U.S. class and subclass, if appropriate, must be given. Where less than the entire disclosure of the reference is involved, the particular pages and sheets containing the parts relied upon will be identified. If the entire disclosure is relied on, the total number of sheets and pages are not required to be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For foreign references include country, number, kind code, date, patentee, and relevant page/sheet citations when only part of the disclosure is relied upon; include IPC subclass/group/subgroup for TCs that file by IPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation data requirements — non‑patent literature (NPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts, abbreviatures, Alien Property Custodian publications, withdrawn U.S. patents, withdrawn U.S. patent application publications, and other non‑patent documents should be cited under the section “Non‑Patent Documents” on the form PTO‑892. In citing a publication, sufficient information should be given to determine the identity and facilitate the location of the publication. For books, the data required by 37 CFR 1.104(d) with the specific pages relied on identified together with the STIC call number will suffice. Titles of books and periodicals SHOULD NOT be abbreviated because an abbreviation will not be sufficient to identify the publication. Bibliographic information provided must be at least enough to identify the publication: author, title and date. For periodicals, at least the title of the periodical, the volume number, date, and pages should be given. These minimal citations may be made ONLY IF the complete bibliographic details are unknown or unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full bibliographic details for NPL (author, title, date, pages); avoid abbreviating titles; include call numbers where useful; use minimal citations only when full details cannot be obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format and retention for electronic documents (WIPO ST.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The format for the citation of an electronic document is as similar as possible to the format used for paper documents of the same type, but with the addition where appropriate of: (A) the type of electronic medium in square brackets after the title (e.g., [online], [CD‑ROM]); (B) the date when the document was retrieved from the electronic media in square brackets following the date of publication (four‑digit year must be given); (C) identification of the source of the document using the words “Retrieved from” and its address where applicable; (D) specific passages of the text could be indicated if the format includes pagination or equivalent internal referencing. Office copies of an electronic document must be retained if the same document may not be available for retrieval in the future. If an electronic document is also available in paper form it does not need to be identified as electronic unless desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite electronic sources per WIPO ST.14: include medium, retrieval date, ‘Retrieved from’ URL/source, and pinpoint passages when possible; retain Office copies for ephemeral online materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for declassified printed matter
rubrics_metrics.description: In using declassified material as references there are usually two pertinent dates to be considered, namely, the printing date and the publication date. The printing date may be considered as that date when the material was prepared for limited distribution. The publication date is the date of release when the material was made available to the public. If the date of release does not appear on the material, this date may be determined by reference to the Office of Technical Services, Department of Commerce. In the use of any of the above noted material as an anticipatory publication, the date of release following declassification is the effective date of publication within the meaning of the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on declassified printed matter, use the date of public release after declassification as the effective publication date for anticipation purposes; seek assistance from OTA/OTS to determine release dates when not shown.
